home.title: Chess,
home.description: A sparse world of squares, where a rook can travel as far as the path stays open. Learn the coordinates, then explore as far as you like.
home.ruleOne: The board extends forever in all four directions.
home.ruleTwo: A square is written as an integer pair: x, y.
home.ruleThree: Checkmate wins. Castling, en passant, promotion and draws follow the selected Classical rules.

setup.title: Choose a way to play
setup.description: Start from the Classical position, then follow the pieces beyond its familiar eight ranks.
setup.botDescription: A seeded opponent with a bounded, legal move policy.
setup.localNote: Hand the device between turns. The board stays in the same orientation.

bot.beginnerHint: Shorter move range with more variation.
bot.clubHint: Looks farther down open lines and values active pieces.
bot.strongHint: Uses the widest candidate range and plays without random noise.

game.serverlessNote: Local games stay on this device. The room server validates every online move.

status.abandonment: Game ended after a player disconnected

board.panHint: Drag to pan · select a piece and enter a coordinate to travel farther

tutorial.title: Learn the open plane
tutorial.description: Try each position yourself. The guide checks your move and explains what changed.
tutorial.tryAgain: That move is legal, but it does not complete this practice. Try the highlighted instruction.
tutorial.success: Well played. The rule is now in action.
tutorial.quizWrong: Look at the king: it is not in check, but it has no legal move.

lesson.sharedCoordinates: Coordinates use exact integer pairs. Negative values are valid, and the same rules work far from the starting position.

coordinates.title: Coordinates and distance
coordinates.summary: Read a square and travel along an open line.
coordinates.description: There is no far edge. Coordinates identify each square exactly, including negative positions.
coordinates.hint: Select the rook, then click the destination or enter x=2 and y=14 below the board.

promotion.title: Pawns reach a fixed rank
promotion.summary: Promote to a queen, rook, bishop, or knight.
promotion.description: The promotion line stays fixed at rank 8 for White and rank 1 for Black.
promotion.prompt: Advance the white pawn one square.
promotion.hint: When it reaches rank 8, choose any of the four promotion pieces.

check.title: Answer a check
check.summary: Move out of check, capture the attacker, or block its line.
check.description: A move is legal only if your king is safe when the move ends.
check.prompt: Move the king or block with the knight.
check.hint: Move the king to safety or place the knight between the rook and king.

mate.title: Win by checkmate
mate.summary: Leave the checked king without a legal reply.
mate.description: Checkmate ends the game immediately. The king does not need to be captured.
mate.hint: Move the queen from (1,7) to (7,7). The king is protected and every escape is covered.

stalemate.title: Recognize stalemate
stalemate.summary: No legal move while not checked means a draw.
stalemate.description: Checkmate and stalemate both have no legal replies. Only checkmate wins.
stalemate.hint: The white king has no legal move, but it is not under attack.

castling.title: Castle to safety
castling.summary: Move the king and rook together in one special move.
castling.description: Castling is allowed only while the right remains and the king does not cross an attacked square.
castling.prompt: Castle kingside: move the king two squares toward the rook.
castling.hint: The rook travels to the square immediately beside the king.

en-passant.title: Capture en passant
en-passant.summary: Capture a pawn that just advanced two squares.
en-passant.description: En passant is available for one turn after an opposing pawn's double advance.
en-passant.prompt: Capture the black pawn on its passed square.
en-passant.hint: The moving pawn lands on the empty square the opposing pawn passed over.

repetition.title: Draw by repetition
repetition.summary: Repeat a position three times to claim a draw.
repetition.description: Position identity includes the side to move, castling rights, and whether en passant changes legal moves.
repetition.prompt: Repeat this four-move king cycle twice. Play both colors in the practice.
repetition.hint: Return both kings to their starting squares, then repeat the cycle once more.

fifty-move.title: The 50-move rule
fifty-move.summary: One hundred quiet half-moves can end in a draw.
fifty-move.description: Pawn moves and captures reset the counter. This position is one half-move from the threshold.
fifty-move.prompt: Make one quiet rook move to reach the 100-half-move threshold.
fifty-move.hint: The counter measures individual moves by either color.

insufficient-material.title: Dead positions
insufficient-material.summary: Some positions cannot produce checkmate and are drawn.
insufficient-material.description: A position is drawn when no possible sequence of legal moves can end in checkmate.
insufficient-material.prompt: Capture the last opposing minor piece. Neither side can mate afterward.
insufficient-material.hint: The rules engine detects when only kings and one minor piece remain.

online.title: Play across the plane
online.description: Create an untimed room and invite a friend with its six-character code. The room is validated by the same rules as local play.
online.createDescription: Start a private two-player game. Share the room link with your opponent.
online.joinDescription: Enter the six-character code from your opponent.
online.invalidCode: Enter a valid six-character room code.
online.roomNotFound: That room could not be found.
online.connectionError: The online service could not be reached. Local games and lessons still work offline.
online.shareHint: Send this code or link to the person joining your game.
online.waitingFor: Waiting for your opponent to join
online.reconnecting: Connection interrupted. Reconnecting to the saved room…
online.moveRejected: The server rejected the last move. The next room update will restore the verified position.
online.noChat: Rooms include moves and draw offers. There is no chat.
online.validated: The server replays every move through the Infinite Chess rules before accepting it.

about.title: About Open Plane
about.description: Open Plane is an independently branded Infinite Chess product using the official Classical starting position and rules profile.
about.rulesText: The square plane has no boundaries. Pieces move as in chess, sliding pieces have no range limit, and pawns promote on ranks 8 or 1. Checkmate wins; stalemate, threefold repetition, the 50-move rule, and insufficient material draw the game.
about.licenseText: The Infinite Chess product source is offered under AGPL-3.0-or-later. The corresponding source includes the web app, rules engine, bot, and online service.
